summary.title: Modern PHP Without a Framework
summary.one_liner: You learn how to bootstrap a small PHP application from interoperable PSR-based packages (Composer autoloading, PHP-DI, Relay middleware, FastRoute, PSR-7 responses and an emitter) instead of using a full framework.
takeaways: PHP apps follow a request/response cycle: the front controller receives each request, the app boots, produces a response, and the response is emitted to the client.
Composer's autoloader (PSR-4) replaces manual include/require statements for loading classes.
A DI container such as PHP-DI supplies constructor dependencies, and disabling autowiring makes the wiring explicit for learning.
PSR-15 middleware, dispatched by Relay, FastRoute handles routing, and PSR-7 Response objects are passed to an emitter that sends them to the web server.
summary.summary: The author argues for building a PHP project without a framework to understand what happens under the hood, and walks through building a minimal app step by step. The tutorial uses Composer autoloading, PHP-DI for dependency injection with autowiring turned off, Relay as a PSR-15 middleware dispatcher, FastRoute via middlewares/fast-route for routing, Laminas Diactoros for PSR-7 messages, and Narrowspark's HTTP Emitter to send responses. It ends with a roughly 44-line bootstrap compliant with PSR-4, PSR-7, PSR-11 and PSR-15, and it links further libraries and a follow-up post. The page was updated in 2019 for PHP 7.2 and to revise its stance on autowiring.
